help.start_intro: A report is one or more pages of elements (text, metrics, tables, charts, card grids, images and shapes) bound to data sources.
help.start_data: **Data** tab: add a data source (what to query), then bind elements to it.
help.start_insert: **Insert** tab: drag an element onto the page, or click it to drop it at the top left.
help.start_select: Select an element to edit it in the panel on the right; select several to align, distribute or style them together.
help.start_preview: **Preview** (eye icon) shows the finished pages with live data, including the extra pages growing tables add.
help.start_save: Save, then use Schedules & webhooks to deliver the report automatically.
help.data_pick: Pick a dataset (playback activity, library items, users...), filter it, and return either rows or a summary (group by + totals).
help.data_params: Filters can compare against a **parameter** (pick @name as the value), so viewers and schedules can change them.
help.data_calculated_body: Row-level expressions computed in the database and usable anywhere a field is: {0}, {1}, {2}, {3}. Write {4} rather than {5} for decimal division.
help.data_after_body: Steps applied to the result in order: filter, calculate a column, top N, pivot, running total, percent of total, rank, change from previous, fill missing dates, sort and limit. These work on totals too, e.g. "users with at least 10 plays".
help.data_join: **Join**: add another source's columns to matching rows (left, inner or full), e.g. this month next to last month per user.
help.data_union: **Union**: stack rows from several sources, optionally with a column naming each row's source.
help.data_nested: Combined sources can build on other combined sources.
help.tokens_intro: Placeholders use double curly braces and work in text, headings, metric labels, card text lines and link URLs. Unknown ones are left as they are, so a typo shows up rather than breaking the report.
help.tokens_page_number: Current page number, counting the extra pages growing elements add
help.tokens_now: When the report was generated, in the report's time zone
help.tokens_ds_field: A column from the first row of a data source (by name or id)
help.tokens_ds_count: How many rows a data source returned
help.tokens_row: Card grid text and link URLs: a column of the card's (or table row's) own row
help.tokens_value: Hyperlink URL templates: the value being linked
help.formats_body: Add {0} after a placeholder: {1}, {2}, {3}. The same formats are offered for table columns and metrics.
help.formats_canvas_count: On the design canvas, {0} only counts design pages; Preview, the viewer and exports show the real total.
help.flow_intro: Turn on **Continue on new pages** (Pages section) for a table or card grid, and rows that don't fit go onto extra pages added after that page, with the table header repeated.
help.flow_header: A dashed green **Header** line appears; drag it (or set Header height). On the extra pages the table starts there.
help.flow_repeat: Everything entirely **above the header line** or **below the table** repeats on every extra page, like page headers and footers: titles, logos, page numbers.
help.flow_between: Everything in between (intro text, metrics, charts) appears on the first page only.
help.flow_first_only: **First page only** keeps a header or footer element off the extra pages.
help.flow_same_breaks: The viewer, Preview and every export break pages in the same places. A report is capped at 500 pages.
help.conditions_intro: Tables, metrics and card grids have a Conditional formatting section. Each rule is a column, an operator and a value, plus the styles to apply.
help.conditions_tables: **Tables**: style the whole row or one column, e.g. red text in Watch time when it's under 60.
help.conditions_metrics: **Metrics**: checked against the first row; styles the value and fill.
help.conditions_cards: **Card grids**: checked per card; styles the card.
help.conditions_order: Rules apply in order; when two set the same thing, the later one wins.
help.cards_intro: One card per row: a poster, backdrop or user avatar, plus up to three text lines. Good for "top 10 movies" or "most active users".
help.cards_media_id: **Media id column**: the column holding the item (or user) id, e.g. ItemId.
help.cards_text_lines: Text lines use {0}, e.g. title {1}, subtitle {2}, value {3}. The "+ column" picker inserts one for you.
help.cards_layout: Set columns, card height, gap, fill, corner radius and a maximum number of cards. A card grid can continue on new pages like a table.
help.cards_link: An optional link per card, e.g. {0}.
help.links_columns: Table columns and metrics: choose the **Hyperlink** format. Leave the URL empty if the value already is a URL, or write a template with {0} and {1}.
help.links_elements: Text and images: set Link to make the whole element clickable. Placeholders work there too.
help.links_encoded: Values inserted after the start of a URL are URL-encoded automatically.
help.links_schemes: Only http, https and mailto links are created; anything else shows as plain text.
help.links_where: Links open in the viewer, HTML/SVG exports and server PDFs. Images (PNG) and in-browser PDFs can't hold links.
help.params_intro: Parameters (Data tab) are values the viewer or a schedule can change: text, a number, a date, yes/no, or a lookup.
help.params_filter: Use one in a filter by picking @name as the rule's value. An empty parameter switches its rule off, which is how optional filters work.
help.params_lookup: A **lookup** is a dropdown of choices from a data source (value column + optional label column), optionally allowing several choices.
help.export_pdf: Sharp text, fonts embedded, clickable links. Best for sharing and schedules.
help.export_png_svg: One page as an image; SVG keeps links.
help.export_html: A standalone page with all pages, fonts and links.
help.export_browser: Captures what you see; no clickable links.
help.export_definition: The design itself, to back up or import elsewhere. Also on the Reports screen. Imports are checked first, and schedules aren't included.
help.export_delivery: Saved reports can be delivered on a schedule or by webhook (generic, Discord or JSON) with Schedules & webhooks in the toolbar.
help.keys_order_keys: Ctrl+] / Ctrl+[ (with Shift: to front / back)
